Student Record Management Application Using SQLite

Framework: React Native (Expo + TypeScript) • Database: Local SQLite (expo-sqlite / students.db)

Objective: Develop a React Native mobile application that stores and manages student information (Add, View, Update, Delete) using a local SQLite database.

1. Requirements Checklist & Verification

Requirement Implementation Detail SQLite Query Executed Status
Add Student Enter student's Name, Course, and Age with validation in StudentFormModal.tsx INSERT INTO students (name, course, age) VALUES (?, ?, ?); Completed
View Students Display all registered students with multi-theme cards & KPI summary metrics in HomeScreen.tsx SELECT id, name, course, age FROM students ORDER BY id DESC; Completed
Update Student Modify Name, Course, and Age of any existing student record UPDATE students SET name = ?, course = ?, age = ? WHERE id = ?; Completed
Delete Student Prompt confirmation dialog (DeleteConfirmModal.tsx) and remove record DELETE FROM students WHERE id = ?; Completed
Local Database Persist all student records locally using SQLite (students.db) in src/database/db.ts CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS students (...); Completed

3. Local SQLite Database Implementation (src/database/db.ts)

export async function migrateDbIfNeeded(db: SQLiteDatabase): Promise<void> { await db.execAsync(` PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS students ( id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, name TEXT NOT NULL, course TEXT NOT NULL, age INTEGER NOT NULL ); `); } export async function getAllStudents(db: SQLiteDatabase): Promise<Student[]> { return await db.getAllAsync<Student>('SELECT id, name, course, age FROM students ORDER BY id DESC;'); } export async function addStudent(db: SQLiteDatabase, input: StudentInput): Promise<number> { const result = await db.runAsync( 'INSERT INTO students (name, course, age) VALUES (?, ?, ?);', input.name.trim(), input.course.trim(), input.age ); return result.lastInsertRowId; } export async function updateStudent(db: SQLiteDatabase, id: number, input: StudentInput): Promise<void> { await db.runAsync( 'UPDATE students SET name = ?, course = ?, age = ? WHERE id = ?;', input.name.trim(), input.course.trim(), input.age, id ); } export async function deleteStudent(db: SQLiteDatabase, id: number): Promise<void> { await db.runAsync('DELETE FROM students WHERE id = ?;', id); }

4. Application Output Screenshots

1. View Students & Local SQLite Database (Initial Seeded Records)

Displays all 5 pre-registered student records loaded from the local SQLite database (students.db) along with the 4 multi-theme KPI summary cards.

2. Add Student — Entering Student Name, Course, and Age

Clicking '+ Add Student' opens the Add New Student modal form. Here we enter Name: 'Kristine Joy Bautista', Course: 'BS Cybersecurity', and Age: '21'.

3. Add Student — New Student Record Saved to SQLite

After tapping 'Save Student', the INSERT INTO students SQL query executes and 'Kristine Joy Bautista' (ID #6) immediately appears at the top of the directory (Total List updated to 6).

4. Update Student — Modifying an Existing Student Record

Clicking 'Update' on Joshua Villanueva (ID #5) pre-populates the form modal with his existing details. We update his course to 'BS Data Science & AI (Honors)' and age to '21'.

5. Update Student — Updated Information Persisted in SQLite

After tapping 'Update Record', the UPDATE students SET ... WHERE id = 5 query executes and Joshua Villanueva's card reflects the updated course and age.

6. Delete Student — Confirmation Dialog Before Removal

Clicking 'Delete' on Angela Mae Reyes (ID #4) prompts the user with a confirmation dialog before executing the permanent SQLite DELETE operation.

7. Delete Student — Record Removed from SQLite Database

After confirming deletion, DELETE FROM students WHERE id = 4 executes and Angela Mae Reyes is removed from the directory (Total List updated from 6 to 5).
